overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation by the DPW Commission or Select Board: the July 14 bridge contract topic was specific enough, no separate vote warning was required, and staff distribution of the contract did not create a deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the July 14 notice topic about a bridge design repair contract was not sufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Because the notice was sufficiently specific, we find that the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice did not warn the public that the Commission might vote on the bridge repair after discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We have consistently explained that it is reasonably foreseeable that a public body may take action and hold a vote following discussion of a topic listed on a meeting notice; the Open Meeting Law does not require that the notice separately indicate the possibility of a vote.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting when a staff member sent a contract to two members who together formed a Board quorum.
allegations.key_passage: we find that there was no deliberation as the contract was sent by Superintendent Batchelor, who is not a member of the Board, and there is no evidence that Mr. Regienus or Mr. Stevens participated in the drafting of the contract or that they discussed the contract outside of a posted meeting.
